Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 3 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Tropical Cyclone "PAOLO"
Issued at: 2:00 PM, 03 October 2025(Friday)

RED WARNING LEVEL: Zambales.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: Serious FLOODING is expected in flood-prone areas.

ORANGE WARNING LEVEL: Bataan.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING is still THREATENING.

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Cavite, Batangas, Pampanga, Bulacan(Hagonoy, Paombong, Bulakan, Bocaue, Meycauayan, Marilao, Obando, Malolos, Calumpit, Balagtas, Guiguinto), Tarlac(Capas, Bamban, San Jose, Concepcion) and Nueva Ecija(Carranglan, San Jose, Lupao, Pantabangan, Bongabon, Rizal, Llanera, Munoz, Talugtug, Cuyapo).
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Quezon, Laguna, Rizal, Metro Manila, Tarlac(Anao, Tarlac City, Gerona, La Paz, Paniqui, Pura, Ramos, San Manuel, Victoria, Camiling, Mayantoc, Moncada, San Clemente, Santa Ignacia), Nueva Ecija(Cabiao, Gapan, General Tinio, San Antonio, San Isidro, Aliaga, Cabanatuan, Gabaldon, General Mamerto Natividad, Guimba, Jaen, Laur, Licab, Nampicuan, Palayan, Penaranda, Quezon, San Leonardo, Santa Rosa, Santo Domingo, Talavera, Zaragoza) and Bulacan(Angat, Baliuag, Bustos, San Jose del Monte, Dona Remedios Trinidad, Norzagaray, Pandi, Plaridel, Pulilan, San Ildefonso, San Miguel, San Rafael, Santa Maria) which may persist within 3 hours.
The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 5:00 PM today.

For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.

REEL: ‘WALKOUT NG GURO, WALKOUT LABAN SA KORAPSYON’

Hundreds of teachers braved the rain in Manila today, October 3, to march against corruption and demand better funding for the education sector in the Philippines. 

Led by the Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) Union and ACT Teachers Partylist, the protest action is part of the continuous movement against government corruption as issues of theft and misuse of public funds remain unresolved. Educators who mobilized ahead of the World Teachers’ Day celebration are one in the call for justice and accountability from corrupt officials.
